title: Division ring extensions and a counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture
summary: We construct a family of division ring extensions and compute their left and right dimensions. In characteristic zero, we obtain a counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture: a hereditary right pure semisimple ring of infinite representation type. For each prime $p\ge3$, we construct in characteristic $p$ a hereditary artinian ring of finite representation type with Coxeter diagram $I_2(p+2)$.

title: Tensor value and the 9/4 bound for matrix multiplication
summary: We give an exposition of OpenAI's recent result that the exponent of matrix multiplication is at most 9/4 valid over every field. Our main tool is a fractional symmetrized variant of the tensor value introduced by Coppersmith and Winograd, used in place of spectral points (tensor characters) in the original proof. We prove a superadditivity inequality for a power of this value on partially direct sums, whose summands share one tensor factor and occupy independent subspaces in the other two. Together with the degenerations of polynomial multiplication tensors from the OpenAI proof, this inequality yields the bound.

title: Supercuspidal and elliptic densities for reductive groups over non-archimedean local fields
summary: Let $\mathbf{G}$ be a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of arbitrary characteristic, with residue field of cardinality $q$, and let $(K_n)$ be a tower of principal congruence subgroups attached to a lattice $\mathcal{L}$ in the Lie algebra. We show that the proportion of the Plancherel mass of the $K_n$-fixed vectors carried by supercuspidal representations is $δ_{\mathrm{ell}}(Λ)+O(q^{-n/4})$, where the elliptic density $δ_{\mathrm{ell}}(Λ)>0$ is the probability that a random element of the dual lattice $Λ$ is nonzero on the Lie algebra of the unipotent radical of every proper parabolic subgroup. For $\mathrm{GL}_d$ this limit was anticipated by Howe. The error improves to $O(q^{-τn/4})$ with an explicit $τ\in(1,2]$, except when $\mathrm{char}\,F=2$ and $\mathbf{G}$ has an isotropic direct factor which over $\bar F$ is a product of adjoint groups of type $\mathrm{B}_d$. We determine when $δ_{\mathrm{ell}}(Λ)=1$, give an explicit bound uniform in $F$ for reductive models, and deduce a bound uniform over the completions of a global field. The proof combines finite Fourier analysis on congruence quotients, a quantitative Sard theorem for parabolic incidence maps and a Jacquet-module argument; it uses neither a classification of supercuspidal representations nor the exponential map.

title: Centres and semisimple deformations of contraction algebras
summary: Let $A_{\rm{con}}$ be the contraction algebra of a $3$-fold flop of an irreducible curve, with genus-zero Gopakumar-Vafa invariants $n_1, \dots, n_l$. We show that $\prod_j M_j(\mathbb{C})^{n_j}$ is the only semisimple algebra to which $A_{\rm{con}}$ deforms. Hence $A_{\rm{con}}$ encodes its Gopakumar-Vafa invariants intrinsically, answering a question of Wemyss. Hua and Toda showed that this deformation exists, and Jelisiejew and Smoktunowicz proved its uniqueness in types A and D. The key step in our proof is that the centre of $A_{\rm{con}}$ has dimension $n_1 + \dots + n_l$. To prove this, we lift the contraction algebra of the universal flop to the Cartan subalgebra, where it becomes a corner of a deformed preprojective algebra. We show that the universal contraction algebra and its zeroth Hochschild homology are free over a polynomial ring, with presentations whose determinants are products of roots. Pulling these presentations back along the arc that classifies the flop gives the count, and recovers Toda's formula for $\dim A_{\rm{con}}$. We also prove Hua and Toda's flatness conjecture, and determine which Gopakumar-Vafa invariants occur in lengths 3 to 6.

title: $\mathrm{X}$-evolution flows/foliations for cluster algebras: partial Bongartz (co-)completions and acyclicity
summary: We first generalize the notion of $\mathrm{X}$-foliation on cluster complexes to the context of cluster algebras. This is a continuous generalization of Keller's green mutation, which was previously introduced in the prequel within a categorical setting. We show that the wall-crossing structure (of possibly higher co-dimension) is encoded by $\mathrm{X}$-supports, which form a partial version of Cao-Gyoda-Yurikusa's Bongartz (co-)completions for cluster algebras. Moreover, we prove that for any cell transversed nontrivially by a fixed $\mathrm{X}$-leaf, its rank is an invariant bounded below by the rank of $\mathrm{X}$. Finally, we prove the acyclicity conjecture for $\mathrm{X}$-foliation, which also implies the compactness conjecture for any $\mathrm{X}$-foliation in finite type cases.

title: Annular webs and Guralnick's conjecture
comment: 39 pages, many figures, Lean verification available, comments welcome
summary: Using annular webs and Kazhdan-Lusztig mu-coefficients, we disprove Guralnick's absolute boundedness conjecture for first cohomology.

title: Plus Constructions and Canonical Induction for Green Categories
summary: We develop canonical induction for Green categories associated with Mackey systems. We establish a change-of-rings framework in which the lower-plus and upper-plus constructions are realized by induction and coinduction of modules. The two plus adjunctions yield the mark morphism, and, when the relevant group orders are invertible in the coefficient ring, Möbius inversion gives an explicit inverse. Using the resulting linearization and tom Dieck maps, we construct a canonical induction map, give an explicit formula for it, and characterize when it is a right inverse of linearization. In the classical setting of Mackey functors, our construction and splitting criterion recover Boltje's results.

title: Long-root $\SL_2$ dual pairs in split exceptional groups: Compact types, cone geometry, and theta correspondence
summary: The paper establishes a case of Howe duality for an exceptional theta correspondence using the ping-pong of types method. To that end, one needs to compute lifts of types of maximal compact subgroups. A brand new ingredient enters here: The graded module of the minimal representations is the coordinate ring of an affine cone whose projectivization is a Grassmannian. Via the filtered Nakayama lemma the problem of lifting types becomes a problem in algebraic geometry: compute certain linear sections of the Grassmannian.

title: Clifford BMW Categories and Conformal Embeddings of Types B C and D
summary: In this paper, we give diagrammatic descriptions of the quantum subgroups coming from conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{g}, \check{h}) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{g}}, 1)$ for $\mathfrak{g}\in \left\{\mathfrak{so}_N, \mathfrak{sp}_{2N}\right\}$, as well as the conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{sp}_{2r + 2}, 2r) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{sp}_{2r + 2}}, 1)$, extending the techniques of Edie-Michell and Snyder which applied to conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{sl}_r, r) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{sl}_r}, 1)$. Our main conceptual innovation is the use of fermion condensation to construct a continuous family of planar superalgebras, which we call the Clifford BMW supercategories. The tower of endomorphism algebras, $CW_n(σ, ε)$ is a combination of Birman Wenzl Murakami algebras and Clifford algebras, much in the spirit of the Hecke Clifford algebras. This tower of algebras appears to be new, and already yields some exciting combinatorics.

title: Structure of derived Hecke algebras with coefficients in torsion-free profinite rings
comment: 51 pages. Revised introduction and exposition; clarified hypotheses and arguments; corrected typographical errors
summary: In this article, we study derived Hecke algebras with coefficients in torsion-free profinite rings regarded as discrete rings. We compare each such algebra with the degreewise inverse limit of the derived Hecke algebras with coefficients in finite rings and with its subalgebra consisting of elements with uniformly finite double-coset support. Under cohomological comparison hypotheses, the natural map to this subalgebra has image given by its degree-zero part and its positive-degree torsion. We describe the kernel in terms of continuous cohomology and prove that it is a divisible square-zero ideal annihilated by every positive-degree element. These comparisons are compatible with Yoneda products, and the action on torsion Ext classes factors through the image. We compute the resulting algebras for the additive group $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and determine the underlying graded abelian groups for $(\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p),\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z}_p))$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}_p$, for $p>3$. The examples exhibit distinct effects of the coefficient topology and the support condition.

title: Incidence algebras and beyond: brick-continuity and generic bricks
comment: 20 pages, no AI used, v2: added some acknowledgments
summary: We will show that the twelve families of minimally representation-infinite incidence algebras are brick-continuous and admit a generic brick, which will be explicitly constructed. After that, reversing the reduction process between posets, we will show that any representation-infinite incidence algebra is brick-continuous and admits a generic brick, which can be explicitly computed using what will be called ''extension functors''. Lastly, a method to apply these results to a broader class of algebras is given.

title: Semibricks and wide subcategories in extended module categories
comment: Added Example 3.22 of a d-FAE closed subcategory which is not a positive torsion class
summary: For $d\geq 1$, we define semibricks and wide subcategories in the $d$-extended hearts of bounded $t$-structures on a triangulated category. We show that these semibricks are in bijection with finite-length wide subcategories. When the $d$-extended heart is the $d$-extended module category $d\mbox{-}\mathrm{mod}Λ$ of a finite-dimensional algebra $Λ$ over a field, we define left/right-finite semibricks and left/right-finite wide subcategories in $d\mbox{-}\mathrm{mod}Λ$ and show bijections with $(d+1)$-term simple-minded collections, generalising the bijections between $2$-term simple-minded collections, left/right-finite wide subcategories and left/right-finite semibricks in $\mathrm{mod}Λ$. We use a relation between semibricks and silting complexes to characterise which mutations of $(d+1)$-term silting complexes are again $(d+1)$-term.

title: A uniform trigonometric R-matrix for the exceptional series
summary: The exceptional series is a finite list of points on a projective line with a simple Lie algebra attached to each point. This list of Lie algebras includes the five exceptional Lie algebras. We give a uniform trigonometric $R$-matrix for the exceptional series in the representation $L\oplus I$, where $L$ is the quantum deformation of the adjoint representation and $I$ is the trivial representation. We construct a sixteen dimensional algebra, $A^\square(\mathit2)$, which interpolates the algebras $\mathrm{End}(\otimes^2(L\oplus I))$ and a 287 dimensional algebra, $A^\square(\mathit3)$, which interpolates the algebras $\mathrm{End}(\otimes^3(L\oplus I))$. The $R$-matrix lives in $A^\square(\mathit2)$ and satisfies the Yang-Baxter equation in $A^\square(\mathit3)$; it interpolates the trigonometric $R$-matrices for the points in the exceptional series.
